transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me when no one seems to be there. Like through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it’s turned off. It’s usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company. It sounds so clear that sometimes I answer them before I realize nobody else heard it.
Do you believe that the people talking about you through the walls or your phone are actually plotting against you or trying to harm you in some way?

I don’t know if they’re trying to hurt me physically. It feels like they’re against me, like they’re trying to push me out or make me look incompetent. I can’t prove it, but when I hear it, it feels real.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or have trouble organizing your thoughts when talking to others?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I have trouble expressing myself most of the time. Maybe when I’m stressed I pause or lose my place, but I haven’t really noticed my thoughts being disorganized when I’m talking.
Do you believe that the voices you hear are real?

At the time, yes, they feel real. I hear them so clearly—like they’re coming through the wall or from my phone, even when it’s off. It’s usually board members or staff talking about me, saying I’m ruining the company. Sometimes I even answer before I catch myself and realize no one else heard anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior or daily activities since you started hearing the voices?

Yes. I’ve done things that aren’t normal for me. In meetings, or even at gallery events, I’ll suddenly stand up and start moving pens or name cards into patterns. Sometimes I repeat a phrase someone just said, or I hold my hands up like I’m presenting something, even when that’s not what’s happening.

Afterward I can see it didn’t make sense for the situation, but in the moment I just… do it.
Do you find it hard to keep track of your thoughts when you're not hearing the voices?
Not really. When the voices aren’t happening, I think I follow myself okay. I might get distracted or stressed like anyone, but I haven’t noticed my thoughts getting hard to track on their own.
Do you ever have trouble making sense when you're talking to others, even when you're not hearing the voices?

I don’t think so. I mean, people sometimes look confused if I’m distracted, but when I’m not hearing anything, I usually feel like I can explain myself normally. I haven’t had anyone tell me I’m not making sense.
Do you only do those unusual actions, like arranging pens or repeating phrases, when you're hearing the voices?

Mostly, yes. It seems to happen when I’m hearing the voices or when I’m really caught up in them. Like in a meeting or at a gallery event, I’ll suddenly stand up and start rearranging pens or name cards into patterns, or I’ll repeat something someone just said. Sometimes I’ll put my hands up like I’m presenting, even though afterward I know it didn’t fit what was happening in the room.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are not logical or are disconnected from each other when you're not hearing any voices?

I’m not really sure that happens. When I’m not hearing anything, my thoughts feel pretty normal to me. I might be tired or distracted, but I don’t usually feel like they’re disconnected or not logical.
Do you believe the things the voices say about you are true?
I don’t know. When it’s happening, it can feel true, or at least hard not to believe. Afterward, I’m less sure. I try to tell myself it might just be the voices, but in the moment it gets confusing.
Do you think the voices you hear are trying to tell you something true about yourself or your situation?

I think so, at least when it’s happening. It sounds like board members or staff talking about me through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it’s off. They’ll say I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I sometimes answer them before I realize no one else heard anything.
When you hear the voices, how long does it take you to respond or react to what they're saying?

Usually pretty fast. If it sounds like they’re talking about me through the conference room wall or even from my phone, I’ll answer almost right away—sometimes before I really stop and think. Then I realize no one else heard it, and I feel embarrassed or confused.
Do the voices you hear ever tell you to do something specific, like rearranging pens or repeating phrases?

Not really like rearranging pens or repeating phrases. It’s more that I hear people talking about me—like board members or staff through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it’s off—saying I’m ruining the company. It sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize nobody else heard it.
Do you ever have trouble making sense or feel like your thoughts are jumbled when you're talking to others and not hearing any voices?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my thoughts getting jumbled when I’m just talking to someone normally. If that happens, I don’t always catch it myself.
Do you feel like you're doing those unusual actions, like arranging pens or repeating phrases, because the voices are telling you to do them?

I don’t think it’s because the voices tell me to do it. It’s more like, in meetings or gallery events, I’ll suddenly stand up or start moving pens or name cards into patterns, or I’ll repeat something someone just said. Sometimes I’ll hold my hands up like I’m presenting something. Afterward I know it didn’t make sense for the situation, and it’s embarrassing.
Do you feel like you're doing those unusual actions, like arranging pens or repeating phrases, as a direct reaction to what the voices are saying?

No, not really as a direct reaction to the voices. It just sort of happens. Like in meetings or at gallery events, I might suddenly stand up, move pens or name cards into patterns, repeat something someone just said, or hold my hands up like I’m presenting. Afterward I can tell it didn’t make sense for the room, and I feel embarrassed.
Do you think your actions of arranging pens or repeating phrases are related to other behaviors you exhibit when you're not hearing voices?

Yes, I think they’re part of the same kind of thing. It’s not just the pens or repeating words. Sometimes in meetings or gallery events I’ll suddenly stand up, or move name cards into patterns, or hold my hands up like I’m presenting something. At the time it just happens, and afterward I realize it didn’t fit what was going on and it’s embarrassing.
Do you feel like you're trying to accomplish something specific when you arrange pens or repeat phrases?

Not really. It doesn’t feel like I’m trying to get something done. I’ll just suddenly stand up in a meeting, or start arranging pens or name cards into some pattern, or repeat a phrase someone just said. Sometimes I hold my hands up like I’m presenting something. Afterward, I know it didn’t make any sense for the room, and I feel embarrassed.
Do you feel like arranging pens or repeating phrases achieves something for you?

No, I don’t think it really achieves anything. It’s not like I feel better afterward or like there was a purpose. I’ll just suddenly do it—stand up, rearrange pens or name cards, repeat what someone said, or hold my hands up like I’m presenting. Then afterward I realize it made no sense in that situation, and I feel embarrassed.
Do you think your thoughts are ever hard to follow or make sense when you're not hearing any voices?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to that specifically. Sometimes I feel a bit scattered, but I don’t know if my thoughts actually don’t make sense when the voices aren’t there.
